brief.headline: Memory Cycle Late-Stage: HBM Supply Easing 2027, DRAM/NAND Peaking, Capex-to-Revenue Gap Widening
brief.summary: <cite index="30-11">TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026</cite>, alleviating the AI accelerator bottleneck into 2027. <cite index="14-2">DRAM contract prices projected +13-18% QoQ Q3 2026, NAND +10-15%, slowing from Q2's 60% jumps</cite> as consumer resistance builds. <cite index="3-15">HBM3E at ~$300/stack (36GB), HBM4 expected ~$500/stack (48GB)</cite>, with <cite index="9-3">Samsung seeking $700/unit for HBM4, 20-30% above prior gen</cite>. <cite index="20-8,23-2,27-3">Hyperscaler capex $600-690B in 2026 (+36-81% YoY), 75% AI-tied</cite>, but <cite index="26-8">capex-to-revenue divergence at 46%, exceeding 2001 telecom bubble's 32%</cite>. <cite index="49-5">SK Hynix holds 60-70% Vera Rubin HBM4 allocation, Samsung 25-30%, Micron remainder</cite> after June certifications.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral-to-short Samsung vs SK Hynix on 3h view. <cite index="44-1,44-7">Both slid 6% today, top-tier investors buying dip</cite>, but <cite index="49-5">SK Hynix's 60-70% Vera Rubin allocation vs Samsung's 25-30%</cite> sustains the leadership gap despite <cite index="48-4,49-2">Samsung passing Nvidia HBM4 qual and starting mass production Feb 2026</cite>. <cite index="52-1,52-5">Samsung HBM4 yield <60% vs SK Hynix 1c DRAM yield at 80%</cite> implies ramp risk. <cite index="1-3">Server DDR5 profitability overtaking HBM</cite> pressures both to rebalance capacity, favoring Samsung's diversified logic/foundry mix. Watch Samsung's ability to convert qual into volume share H2 2026; if yield stays sub-65%, SK Hynix holds pricing power through 2027. ADR discount/premium and FX vol (USDKRW) matter more than fundamentals in next 3h.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="12-1,12-5">Q1 2026 DRAM contracts +93-98% QoQ</cite>, <cite index="14-2">Q3 deceleration to +13-18%</cite> signals peak pricing. <cite index="11-14">DDR4 spot $2.10/Gbit now exceeds HBM3e contract $1.70/Gbit</cite>, an inversion reflecting AI capacity cannibalization. <cite index="7-15">HBM consumes 3x wafer capacity vs DDR5 per GB</cite>. <cite index="12-13">Buyers no longer chasing spot, NAND trading quiet</cite> despite green headlines. <cite index="16-6,16-7">NAND facing structural shortages as manufacturers shift to advanced nodes, pushing contract prices toward historic highs</cite>. Relief unlikely before late 2027 per Gartner.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="3-9,3-11">HBM supply constrained through 2026, lead times 20-26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="3-16">SK Hynix 50-55% market share</cite>. <cite index="48-3,48-4">Nvidia demanding >10 Gb/s HBM4 for Vera Rubin; Samsung passed 10-11 Gb/s qual</cite>, <cite index="48-1,48-5">SK Hynix optimizing for 11 Gb/s tier</cite>. <cite index="50-10">SK Hynix allocated ~70% of Nvidia HBM4 for Vera Rubin</cite>, up from earlier 50% expectations. <cite index="9-3">Samsung pricing HBM4 at $700/unit, +20-30% vs HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="1-5">HBM 2027 rally expected as constrained capacity and rising conventional DRAM margins give suppliers stronger leverage</cite>. <cite index="3-10">Both expanding Icheon/Cheongju/Pyeongtaek fabs, but demand from Nvidia/AMD/hyperscalers outpaces production</cite>. Watch for any Nvidia commentary on Rubin ramp or allocation shifts.

news_pulse.headline: Top investors buy Samsung, SK Hynix on 6% dip as AI capex debate intensifies
news_pulse.implication: Institutional accumulation on weakness; validates long-term AI thesis despite near-term vol. Watch if dip-buying extends or reverses by KRX close.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS gap narrowing to 10% by end-2026 as capacity hits 120-140K wpm
news_pulse.implication: Easing packaging bottleneck supports higher AI accelerator shipments 2H26-2027. Reduces CoWoS premium, shifts focus back to HBM/logic as constraint.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex $600-690B, up 36-81% YoY; 75% AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Demand signal remains robust through 2026, but capex-to-revenue gap at 46% (vs 32% in 2001) raises sustainability concerns. Memory beneficiaries near-term, but watch for spending fatigue 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM Q3 contract pricing slowing to +13-18% QoQ vs Q2's +60%
news_pulse.implication: Peak pricing thesis gaining traction. Server/AI demand still tight, but consumer resistance capping upside. Sequential comps turn easier Q4, raising bar for beats.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 spot ($2.10/Gbit) now exceeds HBM3e contract ($1.70/Gbit)
news_pulse.implication: Profitability inversion favors commodity DRAM reallocation, pressuring HBM capacity adds. Samsung's foundry/logic diversification benefits vs SK Hynix pure-play exposure.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung HBM4 yield <60%, trails SK Hynix 1c DRAM at 80%
news_pulse.implication: Samsung qual win confirmed, but execution risk on ramp. If yield stays sub-65% through Q3, SK Hynix pricing power extends into 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix announce $518B Korea fab cluster; OpenAI 900K wafer/month deal
news_pulse.implication: Capacity announcements signal confidence but also validate tight supply into 2028. Watch for licensing/permitting delays (historical Korea fab timelines run 18-24mo from announcement to groundbreaking).

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks enter bear market: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron -20% from recent highs
news_pulse.implication: Sector-wide repricing on peak-earnings fears despite Samsung's record profit. Confirms momentum exhaustion; tactical fade rallies until supply/demand rebalances or hyperscaler commentary stabilizes.

brief.derivatives_signal: No KOSPI 200 futures or options data in payload. ADR spreads (SSNLF/HXSCL) likely dislocated given 6% KRX cash decline today; watch for arb convergence if US session stabilizes. Implied vol likely elevated on both names post-drawdown; consider calendar spreads if realized vol compresses next 48h. FX overlay: USDKRW strength favors exporters (both names), but hedging programs dampen near-term P&L translation impact.
watch_for_next_3h: Any Nvidia/AMD/hyperscaler commentary on HBM allocation or capex pacing (GTC follow-ups, earnings pre-announcements)
KOSPI close and whether institutional buying persists or reverses; ADR price action in US pre-market
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates (DDR5/NAND) for confirmation of deceleration thesis
Samsung/SK Hynix filings (unlikely sub-3h but monitor DART for any Aug earnings pre-release or capex updates)
